clue.text: In which the early bird lies awaiting the worm?

definitions.text: In which the early bird lies awaiting the worm?

parts.words: In which the early bird lies awaiting the worm?
parts.note: the proverbial early bird catching the worm is pictured as a hidden attacker lying in wait for its prey

explanation.surface: A proverb about the early bird and the worm, retold as a scene of patient waiting.
explanation.definitionFit: A surprise attack launched from a hiding place is what a predator lying in wait springs.

clue.text: Tips guides

definitions.meaning: to tip someone is to give them a hint or recommendation
to guide someone is to counsel or direct them

explanation.definitionFit: Both tipping off and guiding mean offering counsel to someone.

clue.text: The drilling outside is annoying

indicators.note: the drilling word sits outside, wrapping round the word 'The'

parts.note: drilling a hole is boring one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that the roadworks drilling outside the house is irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' looks like it says where the drilling happens; it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that bothers you is irritating you, so the participle works as a synonym.

clue.text: The vicar's address

parts.note: reads like a postal address for a clergyman, but means the talk he gives from the pulpit

explanation.surface: Asking where the vicar lives.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman's address to the congregation is his homily in church.

clue.text: Only males go in at such a meeting

indicators.note: the two pieces are placed inside the letters of 'at', so they go into it

parts.note: taken as written
but can mean only, as in 'but a child'
men are males

explanation.surface: A notice that a certain gathering is for men only.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a men-only gathering; in fact the meeting is where two structures touch.
explanation.definitionFit: An abutment is the point where one structure meets and rests against another, such as a bridge end.

clue.text: A mistake whichever way you look at it

indicators.text: whichever way you look at it
indicators.note: the answer reads identically forwards and backwards, so any direction of reading works

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Someone insisting an error is an error from every angle.
explanation.definitionFit: A boob is informal British slang for a blunder or gaffe.

clue.text: Two trials setting a precedent

parts.note: a test is one trial and a court case is another
a test is one trial and a court case is another

explanation.surface: Two court trials that establish a legal precedent.
explanation.definitionFit: A test case is a lawsuit whose ruling serves as a model for later similar disputes.

clue.text: Pass one bill in ten after amendment

indicators.note: the bill letters are placed inside the rearranged ten
amending changes the order of the letters of 'ten'

parts.note: anagram fodder
a/c, account, is a bill, here a single one

explanation.surface: Parliament passing a bill with ten amendments.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as parliamentary procedure; 'one bill' is A/C, short for account.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass a law is to make it into statute.

clue.text: Beat fellow to the line

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
a gent is a fellow or man

explanation.surface: A runner beating another man to the finishing line.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry this is a straight line just touching a curve.

clue.text: Parties appeal to them

parts.note: political parties court the electorate at election time

explanation.surface: Who it is that festivities attract.
explanation.definitionFit: Political parties campaign to win the support of the electorate.

clue.text: One over the eight?

parts.note: 'one over the eight' is slang for one drink too many, but here it is the person in charge of a rowing eight

explanation.surface: Someone who has had one drink too many.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One over the eight' is a British idiom for being slightly drunk; an eight is also a rowing crew.
explanation.definitionFit: The steersman of a racing boat directs the eight rowers.

clue.text: Game in which Diana and Jack have nothing on, look!

parts.note: Di is short for Diana
a jack tar is a sailor, abbreviated AB (able seaman)
O is zero, nothing
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Diana and Jack playing a game naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have nothing on' suggests nudity but simply joins O to the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A diabolo is a juggling toy spun on a string between two sticks.

clue.text: If you want to use the weighing machine, hurry!

definitions.text: If you want to use the weighing machine, hurry!

parts.words: If you want to use the weighing machine, hurry!
parts.note: a scale is used by standing on it, and the same phrase is slang for hurrying up

explanation.surface: A rushed instruction to someone at the scales.
explanation.definitionFit: Step on it is an idiom for going faster, from pressing a car's accelerator.

clue.text: Cut down chesty complications

indicators.note: complications muddle the letters of 'chesty' into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone recovering from a chest infection with complications.
explanation.definitionFit: A scythe is a long-bladed tool for mowing, so to scythe is to mow down.

clue.text: Workers spread polish

parts.note: worker bees are the classic crossword workers
to wax is to grow or spread

explanation.surface: Workers spreading polish on furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Beeswax is used to shine wooden furniture.

clue.text: Bound to leave something out

definitions.meaning: a bound is a leap or hop
to omit a passage or step

explanation.definitionFit: A light jump is a hop, and passing over material is omitting it.

clue.text: Started job making items of aesthetic worth

indicators.note: making these words into something new rearranges their letters

explanation.surface: Someone who began a job producing works of art.
explanation.definitionFit: This French phrase names small ornaments or curios valued for their beauty.

clue.text: PM comes out of No Ten for a break

indicators.note: breaking these words lets their letters be put together again in a new order

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister leaving Number 10 Downing Street for a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: PM looks like the Prime Minister, but it is post meridiem, after midday.
explanation.definitionFit: PM, post meridiem, covers the hours after noon.

clue.text: Blair is changing note in foreign capital

indicators.note: changing the letters of these words puts them in a new order

parts.note: A is a musical note

explanation.surface: Tony Blair altering his tune while abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link, saying the note joins the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Brasilia is the capital city of Brazil, foreign to a British setter.

clue.text: Lacking respect, notwithstanding

parts.note: regard means respect or esteem
less means lacking, as in 'a year less a day'

explanation.surface: Being disrespectful anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: Regardless means despite everything, in spite of it all.

clue.text: Figure the mob rush out to see

indicators.note: out means the letters of these words are put into disorder

explanation.surface: A celebrity whom the crowd rushes out to see.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhombus is a geometric figure with four equal sides.

clue.text: Guns recoil in game

indicators.note: a gun recoils by kicking back, so the word for guns is read backwards

parts.note: gats are guns in old gangster slang

explanation.surface: Shotguns kicking back during a shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag is a deer, which is game hunted in sport.

clue.text: Collects the rags for recycling

indicators.note: recycling turns these words' letters into something new

explanation.surface: Someone gathering old rags to recycle.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather is to collect things together.

clue.text: Suit to change into?

definitions.meaning: a colour or hat may suit someone, flattering them
a caterpillar turns into a butterfly

explanation.definitionFit: Clothes that flatter you look good on you, and to turn into something is to grow into it.

clue.text: A player — one in new boots

indicators.note: the letter for one sits inside the reworked boots
making the boots new gives their letters a fresh order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A footballer, one wearing new boots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges BOOTS to OBOST, and 'in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboist is a musician who plays the oboe.

clue.text: The gold edging makes this different

indicators.note: gold forms the border, edging round the remaining word

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gold border that makes something stand out.
explanation.definitionFit: Other means distinct or not the same.

clue.text: Treat raw spillage seen in the river

indicators.note: spilling these words scatters their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Untreated sewage spilling into a river.
explanation.definitionFit: This rodent, a vole, lives on riverbanks.

clue.text: Carnival produces a lot of sound

indicators.note: a word is heard rather than read, so its pronunciation gives the answer

parts.note: one's lot is one's fate or destiny

explanation.surface: A carnival making a lot of noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of sound' looks like loudness, but 'of sound' says the word for 'lot' is heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is an outdoor festival or fair.

clue.text: In his eyes, beauty may be seen

definitions.text: In his eyes, beauty may be seen

parts.words: In his eyes, beauty may be seen
parts.note: alludes to the saying that beauty is in the eye of the person looking

explanation.surface: A man who sees beauty everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb places beauty in the eye of the person watching.

clue.text: Doctor got out of bed in a bad mood

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor
rose means got up

explanation.surface: A doctor who got out of bed on the wrong side.
explanation.definitionFit: Morose means sullen and gloomy.

clue.text: Someone not suited for running

parts.note: reads like a poor athlete, but describes a person running naked, not wearing a suit

explanation.surface: An athlete with no aptitude for running.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who dashes naked through a public place, such as a sports ground.

clue.text: Fifteen a side makes this game equal for a start

definitions.text: Fifteen a side makes this game equal for a start

parts.words: Fifteen a side makes this game equal for a start
parts.note: fifteen a side sounds like a rugby team, but it is the score of fifteen all, level after the first points

explanation.surface: A rugby match with fifteen players per team.
explanation.walkthrough: Fifteen a side suggests rugby union; in this game fifteen is the first point won in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Fifteen-all is the level score after each player wins a point in a racket sport.
